fixture_name: Ramp-terminal arterial reconstruction — US preliminary design (MassDOT HSIP municipal RSA, full package)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Ramp-terminal pedestrian exposure, visibility obstruction by vegetation, a four-lane high-speed mid-block crossing, and a recorded past fatality constitute a substantive, well-known high-risk configuration squarely relevant at preliminary design.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Site facts trace to recorded Safety Issue #4 observations while both cited evidence_ids carry verbatim FHWA quotes (EV-US-030 separation-failure mechanism, EV-US-032 signing/marking treatment duty) that directly support the pivotal claim; nothing appears invented.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Framed as a safety_concern under FHWA RSA lineage with TCD adequacy treated as a safety input consistent with FHWA prompt-list practice; the MUTCD observation supports the risk narrative rather than displacing it into a compliance finding.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific, staged, and viable package—immediate MUTCD signage, ADA ramps/delineated crossings in the current design, signalized ramp crossings tied to the planned signal, and mid-block relocation via sidewalk extension—each mapped to an identified deficiency.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians are explicitly identified as the exposed vulnerable-user group with their crossing, accessibility, and visibility needs central to both problem statement and remedies; driver attention conflict is also addressed.

justifications.substance: A genuinely substantive expectancy/decision-point hazard: undefined two-to-one lane transition with no advance signage immediately upstream of an on-ramp mouth creates a credible vehicle-vehicle conflict between late-merging drivers and left-turners exiting the NB ramp, squarely in scope for a preliminary-design RSA.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim (abrupt striping termination and absence of advance lane-reduction signage) is supported by a verbatim quote in EV-US-033; the observed late-merge behavior is flagged as inference-labeled field observation and the confidence basis transparently notes no crash history, keeping claims honestly separated from evidence.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Properly framed as a safety_concern about an operational characteristic with normative_basis_note null, using the EV-US-023 RSA-purpose quote to justify operational-issue identification; no compliance requirement is asserted and safety/compliance categories remain distinct throughout.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable (advance merge signage plus pavement markings located ahead of the on-ramp entrance) and strengthened by carrying a viable design alternative—extending two through lanes past the ramp with its mandatory-right-turn trade-off signed in advance—into the ongoing reconstruction, fitting the preliminary-design stage; minor deduction avoided as MUTCD sign codes are a design-stage detail.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRU relevance at this exact location is explicitly recognized—pedestrians use the adjacent mid-block crosswalk where the lane drop diverts driver attention—and is deliberately routed to companion finding JB-GF12-001, with clear reasoning why this finding's mechanism is vehicle-to-vehicle; this constitutes genuine consideration rather than omission or boilerplate.
